prompt:
Flat sumi-e ink wash painting on aged warm paper. Hand-painted, not rendered. A single isolated subject on plain paper, centred, whole subject in frame. Dark tapering brush outline, flat even ink-wash fill, uniform ambient tone with no visible light source, no cast shadow, no sheen. Monochromatic warm grey from pale paper to near-black ink. Brush character at every edge.

Subject: one gnarled old Japanese cliff pine drawn as a chunky solid object, like a carved stone garden ornament of a pine, seen from a three-quarter angle well above it (looking down at about 40 degrees) so that the top of everything shows. It grows from a rough, irregular, lumpy boulder (not a disc, not a pot, not a tree stump). The trunk is very thick, as thick as a man's waist, twisted, leaning to one side, near-black. Five short, fat branches leave the trunk in five different compass directions: toward the viewer, away from the viewer, left, right, and one straight up. Each branch ends in a foliage pad that is a thick solid dome, like a mushroom cap or a round loaf of bread: we see its whole round top from above and its thick rim, and it is about as deep as it is wide. The pads nearest the viewer overlap and partly hide the trunk and the pads behind. The whole tree is as deep front-to-back as it is wide. Dark grey to near-black pads, no individual needles, no thin twigs, no wispy strokes.

Plain empty paper background and nothing else in the picture: no ground line, no cliff wall, no mist, no clouds, no shadow, no text, no seal. Whole subject in frame with a paper margin all round.
